title: Earl Grey truffles
subtitle: dark chocolate ganache scented with bergamot from steeped Earl Grey tea
excerpt: Earl Grey truffles are dark chocolate ganache made by steeping Earl Grey tea in hot cream for 10 minutes, straining the leaves out, and then pouring the scented cream onto the chocolate. The bergamot note from the tea sits against the dark chocolate without any bitterness. The ganache chills overnight before rolling.
sourceNotes: Tea-infused ganache truffles documented in British artisan chocolate-making from the late twentieth century onward, following the wider interest in flavoured ganaches pioneered by Belgian and French chocolatiers.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth emulsion of chocolate and hot cream. The ratio of chocolate to cream determines whether the ganache is used as a glaze (thin), a soft filling (medium), or a firm truffle (thick).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer, then transfer to a freezer bag for up to 2 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and roll in cocoa before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Bring to room temperature for 20 minutes before serving.

content.text: Earl Grey truffles get their flavour from

made with cream that has been steeped with Earl Grey tea leaves and strained. The bergamot note from the tea comes through clearly against the dark chocolate. The cream must be strained before it goes onto the chocolate so no leaf fragments end up in the ganache.
Heat the cream in a small saucepan over a medium heat until it just comes to the boil. Remove from the heat, add the Earl Grey leaves, and stir briefly. Leave to steep for 10 minutes.
Strain the cream through a fine sieve back into the clean saucepan. Bring back to just below the boil.

Put the finely chopped chocolate and diced butter in a heatproof bowl. Pour the hot strained cream over the chocolate. Leave for 2 minutes, then stir slowly from the centre outward until smooth and glossy.
Press cling film directly onto the surface of the ganache. Chill in the fridge for at least 8 hours, until firm enough to roll.
Sieve the cocoa onto a flat plate. Scoop about a heaped teaspoon of ganache and roll briefly between your palms into a rough ball. Drop into the cocoa and roll to coat. Transfer to a lined tray.
Refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm before serving or storing.

attrs.avoid: Avoid steeping for under 5 minutes; a short steep gives a mild flavour that fades when mixed with the chocolate.
attrs.fix: Steep the cream with the tea leaves for the full 10 minutes, and use a slightly higher quantity of tea. Two rounded tablespoons gives a stronger flavour than two level tablespoons.

attrs.avoid: Avoid cream that is too cool when it goes onto the chocolate; the chocolate will not melt fully and the ganache will be lumpy.
attrs.fix: If the cream has cooled too much after straining, reheat briefly to just below the boil before pouring it over the chocolate. Stir very slowly from the centre.
